interpretation: Statuses describe evidence for each original criterion; this is not a code-coverage, security or production-readiness score. Verified criteria do not close a parent issue.

criteria.text: Specify the initial backend use cases, supported platforms, hardware/storage envelope, data volumes and concurrency.
criteria.assessment: Linux/macOS CI and the bounded retail workload exist. No chosen customer deployment, hardware envelope or concurrency/SLO target is frozen in the architecture programme. Do not invent these from one development host.

criteria.text: Document attacker capabilities and trust boundaries for compiler, VM, natives, editor, Guard, credentials and deployment.
criteria.assessment: SECURITY, Guard and LSP document important trust boundaries. A unified attacker model and supported hostile-execution profiles spanning every listed surface are not established.

criteria.text: Set explicit correctness invariants, latency/throughput/memory budgets, availability expectations and recovery objectives.
criteria.assessment: Correctness checks exist for retail quantities, transactions and retries; production latency, availability, aggregate memory, RPO and RTO acceptance values have not been selected.

criteria.text: Identify which controls belong to the language, runtime, application and deployment; record unsupported scenarios.
criteria.assessment: Language/runtime/operator boundaries and unsupported hostile execution are documented. Deployment ownership and the selected production control allocation remain to be decided.

criteria.text: Freeze representative datasets, provenance/privacy handling, independent oracles and acceptance thresholds before tuning.
criteria.assessment: Public source and corpus hashes, projected-field privacy handling and an independent SQL arithmetic oracle exist. Target-workload representativeness and production acceptance thresholds remain open; this audit independently re-extracts every workbook row.

criteria.text: Retain reviewed design decisions, implementation references, meaningful regression/end-to-end tests, and failure evidence appropriate to this scope.
criteria.assessment: Source and existing regression evidence are linked per acceptance item. The complete scope is not closed; partial coverage, reproduced defects and external requirements are explicitly retained.

criteria.text: For performance/data claims, freeze workload/source identities before tuning, compare with an independent oracle, and report actual limits and unsuccessful trials.
criteria.assessment: Retained real-data evidence is reconciled and the full HTTP path is repeated in this audit, with separate identities, exact oracles and limitations. It still does not qualify production SLOs, large retained state or all requested failure scenarios.

criteria.text: Specify non-forgeable resource authority for database namespaces, filesystem operations and network origins.
criteria.assessment: Host-owned DB namespace grants, package-confined file access and module-declared network origins exist. Network declarations are application source, not operator-issued delegated capabilities; no general resource-capability value/API exists.

criteria.text: Define grant attenuation, delegation, revocation and in-flight operation behavior; applications cannot widen their own authority.
criteria.assessment: DB policy is reloaded before admission; admitted operations may finish after a change, as documented. There is no language-level delegation or attenuation API for these resources.

criteria.text: Enforce authority consistently across transitive calls, native boundaries, caches and concurrent tasks.
criteria.assessment: Effects and DB grants cover the existing native/cache/batch paths. General per-task delegated authority is absent. Malformed deep policy parsing also escapes as RecursionError on Python 3.11 (R3).

criteria.text: Test cross-tenant access, confused-deputy cases, policy changes, traversal/link races and mixed-authority atomic batches.
criteria.assessment: Namespace lookalikes, revocation before cache and mixed-grant atomic batches have tests. A namespace fixture is not authenticated multi-tenant testing; generalized deputy/delegation/race qualification remains open.

criteria.assessment: The retail example documents marker and SKU totals in one batch; the driver limits retries to max_retries (CLI bound 1..1000), backs off and records conflicts. The transfer fixture exercises a multi-key invariant. These are bounded patterns, not a general transaction service.

criteria.text: Verify concurrent histories and independent state models, including stale reads, duplicate delivery and failures around every publication boundary.
criteria.assessment: The 1000-step dictionary model, process transfers, duplicate HTTP race and before/after-replace faults exist. They are not an exhaustive concurrent-history checker or fault injection at every file-write/fsync/publication step.

criteria.assessment: Current descriptor confinement, schema validation, lock, atomic replacement, fsync and authenticated encryption are implemented. Their correctness does not automatically transfer to a new backend or sidecar layout.

criteria.assessment: Retail reduces 541909 source rows to about 0.52 MiB persisted state. No enforced greater-than-RAM retained-state trial exists in this evidence; source-row volume must not be relabeled database size.

criteria.text: Specify deadline propagation, cancellation delivery and commit ambiguity across nested tasks and blocking native calls.
criteria.assessment: Nested cancellation events and join-before-return exist. Blocking natives do not consume a shared deadline; a 10 ms cancellation deadline around 250 ms sleep returns cancellation after the sleep. Large valid i64 sleeps also expose R2.

criteria.text: Bound task queues, request admission, buffered data and retries; define fairness and overload responses.
criteria.assessment: HTTP has 64 workers and a 1024-entry pending queue, limiter storage is bounded and the retail retry loop is capped. This does not impose an aggregate bound on nested parallel tasks or establish fairness/end-to-end admission deadlines.

criteria.text: Implement graceful shutdown/draining and deterministic resource cleanup without abandoning acknowledged durable changes.
criteria.assessment: Signal handling, socket shutdown, draining the pending queue and joins already exist. Joins can wait for blocking natives; HTTP close aborts active connections rather than guaranteeing delivery of acknowledged application outcomes.

criteria.text: Stress slow clients, saturation, cancellation storms, lock contention and shutdown during writes; retain latency and leak evidence.
criteria.assessment: Slow-input, overload recovery, partial-input shutdown, contention and SIGKILL restart are tested. Sustained cancellation storms, all native shutdown states and quantitative descriptor/native-memory leak budgets remain unqualified.

criteria.text: Design authenticated encrypted paging before claiming secure mapped queries; account for decoding and unavoidable copies.
criteria.assessment: AES-GCM-SIV authenticates a complete snapshot; mapping experiments are plaintext. No authenticated page/column query scheme exists, and sealing requires a setup copy.

criteria.text: Compare streaming, buffering and mapping on actual datasets, including enforced beyond-RAM tests, cold/warm conditions and exact results.
criteria.assessment: A retained synthetic 8 MiB comparison favored buffering. It does not satisfy real column-data, encrypted, cold/warm controlled or enforced beyond-RAM qualification.
